In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of eukaryotic gene expression.

the molecular mechanisms that regulate transcription in eukaryotes and how they affect the expression of specific genes and the overall patterns of gene expression in different cell types and in response to different signals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“the enhancers of the human genome have a wide range of functional and mechanistic diversity”.
distal transcription enhancers are diverse in their functional properties, mechanisms of action, and genomic locations.

distal enhancers can be classified into three types, based on the presence or absence of specific transcription factor binding sites, and on their ability to interact with the core promoter via a mediator complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distal enhancers that we have identified are not only functional in vivo but they also play an important role in regulating the expression of the target gene.
distal enhancers are a diverse class of cis-regulatory elements that can be bound by a variety of transcription factors and chromatin regulators.

the distal enhancers of many human genes are highly diverse in sequence, structure, and function, but they are also highly conserved and functionally interchangeable, and that this is accomplished through a common mechanism of action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enhancers that we studied are not all the same.
distal enhancer function is not restricted to a single type of chromatin structure or transcription factor binding.
the enhancer landscape of the genome is far more complex than we previously thought.
